subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or wait for the broader per-session tool-policy design to define the cron boundary?
rationale: This changes a security boundary and public config/default surface, and the correct precedence against existing policy layers cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design cron policy in the session-policy model
options.body: Use the per-session/capability-profile direction to define cron precedence first, then add cron enforcement and docs/tests on that canonical path.

options.title: Add a dedicated cron scope now
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.*` as a narrow global cron policy with explicit precedence over per-job `toolsAllow` where deny must win.

options.title: Document per-job `toolsAllow` only
options.body: Decline new global cron policy and make per-job allow-lists plus delivery safeguards the supported operator workflow.

recommendation.title: Design cron policy in the session-policy model
recommendation.body: Use the per-session/capability-profile direction to define cron precedence first, then add cron enforcement and docs/tests on that canonical path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the prior reviewer on this issue and a recent contributor to the adjacent cron/session capability paths.
